minutes.headline: Task force heard about a free Unitil heat-pump audit, with Turkey Hill the likely first site; only routine votes were taken.
minutes.summary: The committee heard from a Unitil Mass Save representative and a state Green Communities representative about a new, free heat-pump decarbonization audit and the MSBA's new heat-pump program for existing schools. Members then discussed a styrofoam collection bin at Hanford, the Master Plan committee, and the building reuse project. The only votes were approving the February minutes and adjourning.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the February meeting (revised version)

budget_items.topic: Mass Save three-year Energy Efficiency plan
budget_items.what_was_said: The state utility regulator approved the next three-year plan running 2025 to 2027, continuing incentive funding with a focus on electrification.

budget_items.topic: Primary school heat pump project incentive
budget_items.what_was_said: Unitil will contribute incentive funding alongside the state grant, and the dollar amount stays as previously discussed. The application will be updated to the 2025 plan and the gas account supplied.
It is a new free offering, not a grant, available to any commercial customer including schools and municipal buildings.
The METa grant for consulting services was mentioned as due Friday for Green Communities, but the audit was suggested as a better fit.

budget_items.topic: MSBA heat-pump program vs Green Communities
budget_items.what_was_said: A Green Communities representative said large school HVAC projects may suit the MSBA program better than the Green Communities grant, which is smaller.
A member found a grant that might help fund the dumpster or container for styrofoam collection.

decisions.decision: Unitil rep will send the sign-up link; the chair will coordinate dates with the schools and request audits, with Turkey Hill the priority.
Agreed to test the audit at both Turkey Hill and the municipal center to see whether the report is detailed enough.
The Green Communities rep will resend the MSBA program information to the chair.
Chair will contact the West Boylston facility first about the styrofoam container before involving the vendor.
Next meeting aimed for Monday April 7th.

what_happened.line: The task force heard from a Unitil Mass Save representative about a new, free heat-pump decarbonization audit open to schools and municipal buildings.
Members agreed to try the audit at both Turkey Hill and the municipal center to see whether the report is detailed enough; the chair will request audits and coordinate dates.
A Green Communities representative said large school HVAC projects may fit the MSBA heat-pump program better than the smaller Green Communities grant.
The task force discussed a styrofoam collection bin at Hanford; the chair will contact the West Boylston facility before involving the vendor.
The only votes were approving the February minutes and adjourning; the next meeting is aimed for Monday, April 7th.

why_it_matters: A free audit is a way to learn what heat-pump work at the schools and municipal center would involve before the town is asked to fund any of it.
Which program pays for a school heat-pump project (MSBA, Green Communities or the utility incentive) decides how much of the cost falls on the town, and that choice is still open.
